SurfaceKind.doc: The five WebView2 surfaces. All load the same UI bundle; the route (#/dock, #/menubar, #/overlay, #/desktop, #/settings) selects the surface. 'settings' is a normal resizable window (System-Settings-like preferences + onboarding), opened from the Apple menu / tray icon.

MonitorInfo.$doc: A display. boundsPx/workAreaPx are in virtual-screen PHYSICAL pixels; every other geometry in the protocol is in DIPs of the surface that owns it.
MonitorInfo.name: string

devicePath.doc: Monitor device interface path (IDesktopWallpaper.GetMonitorDevicePathAt form). id = MonitorIdentity.IdFromDevicePath(devicePath).

FeatureFlags.$doc: Experimental features; all off by default and individually switchable in settings.general.features.

SurfaceReadyParams.$doc: Informational only: the host IGNORES surface/monitorId for identity (it uses the SurfaceId it assigned when it attached the WebView) and rejects a mismatch with badRequest.

SurfaceInit.$doc: Everything a surface needs to render its first frame. Returned by surface.ready; the host then also pushes the current state events for the surface.

glassOverflow.doc: True if the host can restrict the backdrop to 'rects' while 'hitRects' stay un-blurred. If false the UI must keep ALL dock content (magnified icons, tooltips) inside the glass rects (grow the panel instead of overflowing it).

barThickness.doc: Dock only. DIP extent of the always-visible bar measured from the docked screen edge (EXCLUDES magnification headroom and tooltips). The host reserves ceil(barThickness x monitor scale) physical px through the AppBar when settings.dock.reserveSpace && !autoHide; null keeps the previous value.

patch.doc: RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch applied to the serialised current Settings: objects merge recursively (including map<> fields), arrays and primitives replace, null DELETES the key (nullable -> null, non-nullable -> its default, map entry removed). A key that does not exist in Settings -> badRequest naming the path. 'version' is never patchable. Patch <= 256 KB. The host validates/clamps (see docs/IPC.md section 12) and returns the stored value; settings.changed carries the same value.

SurfaceShapeParams.$doc: The UI's glass panels (and interactive-but-not-glass areas), in DIPs relative to the window client area.

rects.doc: Glass panels (rounded rects): visible, interactive and backed by the blur/acrylic backdrop.

hitRects.doc: Visible and interactive but NOT glass (magnified dock icons, tooltips that overflow the panel). Included in the window region and hit-testing, excluded from the backdrop where the host can restrict it (see SurfaceInit.glassOverflow). May be empty.

blur.doc: Master switch: false = no backdrop (reduceTransparency, or the UI wants flat panels).

locale.doc: Effective UI locale ('en' | 'ru' | ...), already resolved from settings.general.language.

surface.resize.doc: Dock only: the UI asks for a window of this DIP size (bar + headroom); the host clamps, keeps it centred on its edge, and re-reserves the AppBar for barThickness only. Sent when content/headroom changes.

surface.log.doc: UI log line, forwarded to the host log.

surface.visibility.doc: The host shows/hides the surface window (fullscreen app, overlay open, ...).

settings.changed.doc: Full settings after any change (from any surface, file edit, or reset).

surface.shape.doc: The UI reports its glass panels. Host contract (normative): window region = union(rects, hitRects) in physical px (DIP x scale) via SetWindowRgn for dock/menubar only (never overlay/settings; desktop has no region); backdrop = DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE (acrylic/transient) on Windows 11 22H2+ (undocumented accent only behind a feature flag on older builds); DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow MUST NOT be used (it does not blur since Windows 8). Re-send whenever panels move/resize; the host debounces.

settings.navigate.doc: Settings window is already open: switch to this page.

locale.changed.doc: The effective UI locale changed (settings.general.language). SurfaceInit.locale carries the initial value.

surface.ready.doc: First message every surface sends. After replying the host pushes all current state events to this surface.

settings.patch.doc: Deep-merge, validate/clamp, persist, broadcast settings.changed, return the result.

settings.openWindow.doc: Open (or focus) the settings window, optionally on a page.
